sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Aishwarya Pratap Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mahima Maurya Kushwaha,Mukesh Kumar Kushwaha
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.
List revised.

2. Heard Sri Aishwarya Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Mukesh Kumar
Kushwaha, learned counsel for the first informant, Sri Ajay Singh, learned A.G.A. and perused the
material on record.
3. Learned A.G.A. has served a copy of counter affidavit to learned counsel for the applicant today in Court which is taken on record.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant states that he does not intend to file any rejoinder affidavit in response to the counter affidavit of the State.

1
5. Learned counsel for the first informant submits that his counter affidavit is under preparation.
6. Records show that previously on 14.6.2023 learned counsel for the first informant was granted time to file counter affidavit in the matter.
One month and five days has elapsed since then and still no counter affidavit has been filed by the learned counsel for the first informant.
The Court thus proceeds to hear the matter by closing the opportunity to file counter affidavit.

7. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Rajat, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 319 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S. Bannadevi, District Aligarh.

8. The F.I.R. of the present case was lodged on 3.5.2022 by Shyoraj Singh against the applicant Rajat, Dushyant Singh, Mithlesh, Vishal and Jagriti alleging therein that his daughter was married to the applicant on 12.12.2021.
He had spent Rs.20 lakh in the marriage by giving a lot of gifts.
There was demand of Rs. 5 lakh and Swift car as dowry due to which his daughter used to be tortured physically and mentally.
On 1.5.2022 he received a call from his daughter Geeta who stated that she is being tortured by her in-laws and any untoward incident can happen with her.

He along with his son Manish reached her matrimonial house where he consoled his daughter and also her in-laws but on 2.5.2022 his elder daughter received a phone call on her mobile phone that Geeta is seriously ill and is admitted in Medical College.
He reached J.N. Medical College and found that due to demand of dowry Geeta has been given some poisonous substance.

She died at about 09.30 P.M.
9.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that although the applicant is husband of the deceased but he has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is argued that it is a case of suicide and the deceased committed suicide as she wanted to marry one Amit but since her parents and her brother threatened her she forcefully got married to the applicant against her will.
Para-9 of the affidavit has been placed before the Court to buttress the said argument.

It is argued that the deceased was taken to J.N. Medical College where as per patient note was admitted by Rajat Singh who is husband of the deceased, who disclosed to the doctor that patient was apparently well on 2.5.2022 at 11.00 am when she developed multiple episodes of nausea and vomiting.
The doctor further noted in specific terms that she herself told that she took some unknown substance after which they took her to Private Hospital from where the patient was referred to J.N.M.C.
It is argued that the same would go to show that the applicant is not involved in the present case and he has tried level best to save his wife.

It is argued that the post mortem examination report of the deceased was conducted and there was no internal injury seen on her body and cause of death could not be ascertained and hence viscera was preserved.
In the viscera report "Organochloro Insecticide Poison" was found.

It is argued that investigation in the matter has concluded and charge sheet has been submitted against the applicant, Dushyant Singh(father-in-law) and Mithlesh (mother-in-law) whereas co-accused Vishal and Jagriti were exonerated by the police which would also go to show the untruthfulness of the prosecution case.
It is argued that since investigation in the matter has concluded and charge sheet has been submitted there are no chances of the applicant tempering with the evidence or threatening the witnesses.
It is argued that the applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para-58 and he is in jail since 4.7.2022.

2 10.

Per contra, learned AGA and learned counsel for the first informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the deceased died in her matrimonial house within seven years of marriage and death is unnatural.

It is argued that in the F.I.R. and even in the statement of the first informant recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the applicant, who is the husband of the deceased, is named and there are allegations of demand of dowry of Rs.5 lakh and a swift car and due to non fulfillment the deceased has been done to death.
It is argued that even the conduct of the applicant and his family members was not above board as prior to the incident the deceased was being tortured and harassed by them.

An information about it was given by the deceased to her parents and the first informant reached her matrimonial house and consoled her and her in-laws but even then they did not mend their way and on the very next day gave her some poisonous substance and she died.
It is argued that therefore, the bail application of the applicant should be rejected.
11. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
Marriage of the deceased with the applicant was solemnized on 12.12.2021.
The incident in the present matter is of 2.5.2022 for which the F.I.R. was lodged on 3.5.2022.
The incident has taken place within five months of marriage.
The deceased was in her matrimonial house where she become unwell.
In so far as the medical reports are concerned the same are subject matter of trial and have to be appreciate after evidence.
The deceased was found to have died due to some poisonous substance which has been found in her viscera report.
12. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
13. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.
(Samit Gopal,J.)
